conviction_note: Nothing decisive found. The company-level evidence is the Q2 guide itself (revenue down high single digits, adj. EPS -$0.03 to -$0.01) against a consensus that sits at or slightly above it. Counterparties lean mildly negative for UA's North American wholesale (Nike NA wholesale +9%, adidas NA +12%, Puma NA -17%, Columbia US wholesale shipments late). Against that, about 35-38% of float is short (65M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up from 53.5M) and the stock ran +11% in 20 days and +8.5% on 2026-11-04 with no news. So p_up is 47 on an abs move of 10.5, giving -0.63, a little smaller than the findings' -0.9 sum because the squeeze pulls p_up toward 50.
bar: Revenue: company guide for Q2 FY27 is a high-single-digit decline on $1.33B (about $1.21-1.24B). Consensus is $1.22-1.23B (Benzinga, via search snippet) and -7.7% y/y (StockStory, https://www.financialcontent.com/article/stockstory-2026-11-5-under-armour-earnings-what-to-look-for-from-uaa). Adj. EPS: company guide is -$0.03 to -$0.01 (https://finviz.com/news/379329/under-armour-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-results-maintains-full-year-profitability-outlook-while-updating-revenue-expectations). EPS consensus is DISPUTED: Earnings Whispers $0.00 and Benzinga $0.01, both above the guide, from snippets only, so every EPS-dependent finding is capped small. FY27 adj. EPS guide is $0.08-0.12 and adj. operating income $140-160M, which includes about $70M of IEEPA refunds. UBS expects the FY guide to be held (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/ubs-lowers-under-armour-stock-price-target-to-8-on-weak-sales-93CH-4979946, 2026-10-28).
positioning_check: Short interest is crowded. Fintel: 65.1M shares, 37.9% of float, 11.7 days to cover (NYSE figure, settlement undated, page read 2026-11-05, https://fintel.io/ss/us/uaa). CurvedTrading/FINRA via search snippet: 65.1M shares and 6.0 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement, against 53.5M at 2026-09-15. MarketBeat (snippet) says short interest recently fell 9.2%. The 25-delta skew is null in the baseline. Put/call open-interest ratio is 0.36, so open interest is call-heavy. The ATM spread is 67% of mid. The event-implied move is 10.31% (Bloomberg-cited 13% on 2026-10-30, UBS ±9.5% on 2026-10-26). The stock exceeded its implied move in 6 of its last 8 prints (Investing.com, 2026-10-30). There was a squeeze precedent on 2026-02-06 (+20%, with short float then 41%). Strategic holder: Frasers Group owns 8.8% of Class A (13G, event 2026-09-24).

findings.finding: The EPS bar sits above the company's own guide. Q2 FY27 adj. EPS was guided to -$0.03 to -$0.01 on 2026-08-07, while consensus reads $0.00 (Earnings Whispers) to $0.01 (Benzinga). A print at the guide midpoint (-$0.02) would therefore be a miss against consensus. UBS says tariff benefits and cost cuts should still get EPS in line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-08-07): adj. EPS $0.05 against $0.02 consensus, with revenue slightly light. The stock fell 4.5% close to close (about -10.5% intraday per Investing.com). EPS beats on this name have been sold when revenue is soft.
findings.why_not_priced: Weakly unpriced at best. The gap between guide and consensus is visible on any terminal, but the consensus figures disagree with each other, and UBS (Buy) frames the quarter as in line. Had the market priced a below-consensus print, the stock would not have rallied 16.6% in a month (against 8% for the sector) into it. Capped small because the EPS bar is disputed.
findings.independence: UBS preview (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/ubs-lowers-under-armour-stock-price-target-to-8-on-weak-sales-93CH-4979946) expects EPS in line, which cuts against this finding.

findings.finding: The two largest brands regained US wholesale share during UA's Jul-Sep quarter, and the third-tier brand lost it. Nike's NA wholesale grew +9% in Jun-Aug (reported 2026-10-01). adidas grew NA revenue +12% c.n. in Q3 2026 (2026-10-29). Puma's North America fell 17.2% c.n. in Q3 2026 (2026-10-30). UA's own NA was -9% in Q1 and is guided down high single digits for Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: North America is the line this stock trades on. May 2026 (-17%) and Aug 2025 (-18%) came on weak NA outlooks. In Nov 2025 NA came in at -8% against a guided low-double-digit decline, and the stock moved only -1.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: These are peer prints that landed after UA last spoke on 2026-08-07, and consensus revisions were flat over the last 30 days (StockStory). If the market had priced share loss to Nike and adidas at Dick's and Academy, NA estimates would have been cut and the stock would not have outrun the sector by 8 points. This is a proxy: UA has not confirmed it, and the company already guides NA down high single digits, so only a miss beyond the guide counts. Net of the rest of the company: international was +5% in Q1, but EMEA is guided down low double digits in Q2.
findings.independence: Puma Q3 2026 (https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/news/EQS-News-PUMA-Q3-2026-sales-performance-improves-sequentially---FY-2026-outlook-updated-747cfc04-4107-49cb-ba7a-38d36642c441), NA -17.2% c.n. adidas Q3 2026 (https://fashionunited.com/news/business/adidas-raises-full-year-profit-outlook-to-2-5-billion-euros-after-record-q3/2026102975440), NA +12%. Three separate documents, all industry proxies.

findings.finding: UA's largest channel partners were mixed in May-July. Dick's comps were +4.9%, but Foot Locker pro forma comps were -3.6% and Dick's cut Foot Locker's comp guide to -2% to flat (2026-08-25). Academy's footwear and apparel comps were lower, with total comps -0.4% (2026-09-09).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No release ties UA's reaction to retailer comps directly. Wholesale was $638M (-2%) of $1.1B in Q1.
findings.why_not_priced: These retailer prints are public and partly overlap the period UA guided on 2026-08-07, so they are mostly priced. They are a broad series rather than UA's own number. Had the market read them as negative for UA, estimates would have moved; they did not.
findings.independence: Academy Q2 FY26 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001817358/000181735826000146/exhibit991pressreleaseq220.htm), footwear and apparel comps lower. A different document from the Dick's release.

findings.finding: UBS channel checks show UA sales trends still weak (note of 2026-10-26, stock then $4.70). UBS expects tariff benefits and cost cuts to deliver an in-line Q2 and the FY27 adj. EPS guide of $0.08-0.12 to be held. It sees balanced risk and expects a move below the ±9.5% then implied.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide held or cut has driven the large moves: May 2026 -17% on a weak initial FY27 guide, Feb 2026 +20% on a raised outlook, Aug 2026 -4.5% when the revenue guide was cut and EPS held.
findings.why_not_priced: It is on the wire, so largely priced. What it adds is that sell-side checks say revenue is weak, while the stock has since risen about 15% from $4.70 to $5.415, so the price now sits above the level where the 'weak sales, in-line EPS' view was written.
findings.independence: Consistent with the peer read in finding 2 (a different source type: sell-side checks rather than peer filings).

findings.finding: Short interest is crowded and was building into the quarter. At the 2026-09-30 settlement it was about 65.1M shares, against 53.5M at 2026-09-15 (FINRA via CurvedTrading snippet). Fintel shows 37.9% of float and 11.7 days to cover. The Feb 2026 print squeezed +20% with short float then 41%. Open interest is call-heavy (put/call 0.36).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-02-06: +20.4% on a beat and raised outlook into about 41% short float. 2024-11-07: +28.4% per Investing.com. Both large up-moves came with a crowded short.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the +11% 20-day run-up and the reported 9.2% drop in short interest suggest some covering already. Even so, 6-12 days to cover means any guide-hold or clean beat meets forced buying, and a weak print meets a short base already positioned for it. If the squeeze were fully priced, short interest would have collapsed rather than sat near 65M.
findings.independence: Short squeeze precedent article (https://www.itiger.com/news/2609545590, 2026-02-07), 41% short float then. A separate source.

findings.finding: Frasers Group (Mike Ashley) disclosed a strategic 8.78% stake (16.58M Class A shares) in a 13G filed 2026-10-01, event date 2026-09-24. Plank welcomed it publicly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; this is a first-time strategic holder.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it was disclosed a month ago and widely reported. It matters at the print only as a holder who may add on weakness and as a reason shorts may cover. Plank's roughly 65% voting control rules out a bid, so it is not an M&A floor.
findings.independence: Retail Gazette (https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/sports-direct-frasers-stake-under-armour/) reports the same stake, so it is the same fact.

findings.finding: The CFO, Reza Taleghani, bought 18,656 Class A shares in the open market at $5.37 on 2026-08-11 (about $100k). Holdings after: 87,621.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public on EDGAR and small. It is one data point that the CFO saw no deterioration as of four days after guiding. It was bought at roughly today's price, so it says nothing about value above $5.4.

findings.finding: Plank received 2,165,533 performance RSUs (Class C) on 2026-08-26. They vest only if Class C averages at least $5.77 over 60 consecutive trading days before 2030-03-31.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an incentive alignment fact with no direct path to this quarter's number. Filed so the panel can see it; sized 0.

findings.finding: The stock ran into the print with no company news. It rose +16.6% in the month to 2026-11-04 against +8% for the apparel sector (StockStory), and closed +8.5% on 2026-11-04 at about $5.58 on roughly 1.6x normal volume with no identified cause. The baseline shows +7.9% over 5 days and +11.0% over 20 days. That raises the bar for a name whose last two prints were sold (-17.0% and -4.5%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-07: an EPS beat with the revenue guide cut, -4.5%. 2026-05-12: -17.0%. Run-ups into this name's prints have not protected it.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is itself the price. The point is that expectations now embed something better than the 'weak sales, in-line EPS' view UBS wrote at $4.70. If the rally were short covering already finished, short interest would be well below 65M; it is reported down only about 9%. Shrunk for the crowded short.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline tape (run_up_5d_pct +7.87, run_up_20d_pct +10.96) agrees; it is separate data.

findings.finding: Columbia's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-29) says lower US net sales 'reflected later shipments of Fall '26 wholesale orders'. If that timing is industry-wide, UA's Jul-Sep quarter, which carries fall wholesale shipments, would also see US wholesale shipments land late.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No UA release on wholesale timing found. UA guided EMEA down low double digits in Q2 after +12% in Q1, which suggests timing already sits in UA's guide for at least one region.
findings.why_not_priced: It is one peer's footnote, not aggregated into UA previews. A timing shift is a deferral that a guide-holding company can explain away, so the reaction effect is small. Columbia also beat and raised overall, which cuts the sector read the other way.

findings.finding: Late-October peer reactions in apparel were positive. VF Corp rose +7.6% on a 1.1% revenue beat (StockStory). Columbia beat its own guide and raised its FY26 sales and EPS outlook on 2026-10-29. adidas raised its FY profit outlook on 2026-10-29.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is the likely backdrop to UA's sector-beating run. It is filed because it is a sourced fact pointing the other way from finding 2.
findings.independence: StockStory peer section (https://www.financialcontent.com/article/stockstory-2026-11-5-under-armour-earnings-what-to-look-for-from-uaa) for VF. A different document.

outside_window.finding: The Fiscal 2025 Restructuring Plan (about $305M total, $266M incurred) is to be substantially complete by 2026-12-31. Any FY28 margin framing would come later.

baseline_tension: The mild negative lean (proxies, sell-side checks and a bar above the guide) cuts against the +11% run-up, call-heavy open interest and a crowded short; skew is unavailable. The squeeze risk is why p_up is 47 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar): the EPS-bar finding was capped from -0.5 to -0.4 because the two consensus sources disagree with each other and with the guide.
Rule 7 (crowded short, about 38% of float): the negatives were shrunk. Peer share-shift went from -0.8 to -0.6, run-up from -0.8 to -0.6, Columbia timing from -0.4 to -0.3. p_up moved from 46 to 47.
Rule 5 (proxy): the peer and retailer findings were left small and labelled as proxies; no further cut, so the same concern is not applied twice.
Rules 1 and 2: the run-up finding already carried the 'this name sells beats' history; unchanged.
The squeeze, Frasers, CFO-buy and RSU findings were left standing.
